content:
<Rep. Jamie Raskin>: This is another immigration bill that rips a crime from the headlines and makes it a deportable offense without requiring a conviction. This bill is particularly bizarre. It makes the commission of a variety of fraud offenses a deportable offense, without requiring a conviction. But conviction of a fraud offense is already a deportable offense--it is considered a Crime Involving Moral Turpitude (CIMT) and a specifically enumerated aggravated felony--the conviction of either of which subjects any immigrant to deportation.
In the past, the Majority claimed these bills were necessary to resolve ambiguity in the law. But that is not an issue here. Section 101(a)(43) of the Immigration and Nationality Act lists fraud as an aggravated felony--a deportable offense. Even more starkly, we have longstanding Supreme Court precedent from more than 70 years ago that makes it clear that fraud is a CIMT, and therefore a deportable offense.
In Jordan v. De George, a Supreme Court case decided in 1951, the Court held that ``The phrase `crime involving moral turpitude' has without exception been construed to embrace fraudulent conduct.''\1\ The opinion stated unequivocally that, ``In every deportation case where fraud has been proved, federal courts have held that the crime in issue involved moral turpitude.''\2\ The Court even addressed the idea of statutory ambiguity, declaring, ``Congress sufficiently forewarned respondent that the statutory consequence of twice conspiring to defraud the United States is deportation.''\3\
\1\Jordan v. De George, 341 U.S. 223 (1951).
\2\Id.
\3\Id.
It could be that the Majority has such a distaste for due process, that they simply could not pass up the opportunity to attack it. After all, the initial version of this bill did require a conviction, but the Amendment in the Nature of a Substitute adopted at markup removed that requirement. Representative Pramila Jayapal (D-WA) offered an amendment that would return the bill to its original form by requiring a conviction before one could be rendered deportable. Republicans rejected this amendment.
It is also hard to believe that the Majority is putting forward this bill out of a sincere desire to combat fraud. After all, President Donald Trump himself is the only President to be convicted of fraud by a jury of his peers. He was convicted of 34 counts of falsifying business records with the intent to defraud, including an intent to commit or conceal a conspiracy to promote a presidential election by unlawful means. As President, he has pardoned and commuted sentences for convicted fraudsters. Additionally, the Administration's actions do not show any actual focus on fighting fraud. In fact, due to the Trump Administration's single-minded focus on immigration enforcement, the Federal Bureau of Investigation directed its agents to deprioritize white collar crime and devote their time to immigration enforcement.\4\ As a result, prosecutions of white-collar crimes, which include a variety of fraud offenses, was down more than 10% in 2025, compared to white-collar prosecutions in the last year of the Biden Administration.\5\
\4\Federal Prosecution of White-Collar Crimes Receiving Less and Less Attention, TRAC (May 23, 2025), https://tracreports.org/reports/ 760/.
\5\Id.
This bill is simply another effort to follow the narrative pushed by the Administration: a fake focus on fraud that ignores all the real fraud we can see before us. The Administration used fraud as a predicate to send thousands of federal agents to recklessly patrol Minneapolis and the surrounding areas. Renee Nicole Good, a U.S. citizen and mother of three, is dead because an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot her three times as she attempted to drive away from him. Now, the Administration cannot stop lying about the incident.
There is a quote from George Orwell's seminal work 1984 that has been making the rounds in response to the Administration's all-out war on the truth: ``The Party told you to reject the evidence of your eyes and ears. It was their final, most essential command.''
Every day, this Administration pushes lies to try to get us to ignore reality. It is constantly perpetrating a fraud upon the American people. Now Republicans want us to believe that they are the champions of combatting fraud. The American people are not stupid.
I oppose this legislation, and I urge my colleagues to do the same.
Jamie Raskin,
Ranking Member.
